import pandas as pd


def _nullable_eq(a, b):
    a_na = pd.isna(a)
    b_na = pd.isna(b)
    if a_na and b_na:
        return True
    if a_na or b_na:
        return False
    return a == b


def run(inputs: dict) -> dict:
    dim = inputs["dim_customer"].copy()
    stg = inputs["stg_customer"].copy()

    # Ensure proper dtypes for working columns
    dim["eff_start_date"] = pd.to_datetime(dim["eff_start_date"])
    dim["eff_end_date"] = pd.to_datetime(dim["eff_end_date"])
    dim["is_current"] = dim["is_current"].astype("int64")
    dim["customer_id"] = dim["customer_id"].astype("int64")

    stg["update_date"] = pd.to_datetime(stg["update_date"])
    stg["customer_id"] = stg["customer_id"].astype("int64")

    # Step 1: Deduplicate STG_CUSTOMER to the latest record per customer_id
    # by update_date; on ties, keep the record with the greater (name, segment)
    # pair under lexicographic comparison.
    stg_sorted = stg.sort_values(
        by=["customer_id", "update_date", "name", "segment"],
        ascending=[True, False, False, False],
        kind="mergesort",
    )
    stg_dedup = stg_sorted.drop_duplicates(subset=["customer_id"], keep="first")
    stg_dedup = stg_dedup.sort_values(by=["customer_id"], kind="mergesort").reset_index(drop=True)

    # Work on a mutable copy of dim rows, tracking index of current row per customer
    dim = dim.reset_index(drop=True)

    new_rows = []

    for _, s in stg_dedup.iterrows():
        cust_id = s["customer_id"]
        s_name = s["name"]
        s_segment = s["segment"]
        s_update_date = s["update_date"]

        mask = (dim["customer_id"] == cust_id) & (dim["is_current"] == 1)
        matching_idx = dim.index[mask]

        if len(matching_idx) == 0:
            # No current row exists -> insert new
            new_rows.append({
                "customer_id": cust_id,
                "name": s_name,
                "segment": s_segment,
                "eff_start_date": s_update_date,
                "eff_end_date": pd.NaT,
                "is_current": 1,
            })
        else:
            idx = matching_idx[0]
            c_name = dim.at[idx, "name"]
            c_segment = dim.at[idx, "segment"]

            name_changed = not _nullable_eq(c_name, s_name)
            segment_changed = not _nullable_eq(c_segment, s_segment)

            if name_changed or segment_changed:
                # Expire current row
                dim.at[idx, "eff_end_date"] = s_update_date
                dim.at[idx, "is_current"] = 0

                # Insert new version
                new_rows.append({
                    "customer_id": cust_id,
                    "name": s_name,
                    "segment": s_segment,
                    "eff_start_date": s_update_date,
                    "eff_end_date": pd.NaT,
                    "is_current": 1,
                })
            # else: no change, do nothing

    if new_rows:
        new_df = pd.DataFrame(new_rows, columns=[
            "customer_id", "name", "segment", "eff_start_date", "eff_end_date", "is_current"
        ])
        new_df["customer_id"] = new_df["customer_id"].astype("int64")
        new_df["eff_start_date"] = pd.to_datetime(new_df["eff_start_date"])
        new_df["eff_end_date"] = pd.to_datetime(new_df["eff_end_date"])
        new_df["is_current"] = new_df["is_current"].astype("int64")

        result = pd.concat([dim, new_df], ignore_index=True)
    else:
        result = dim.copy()

    result = result[["customer_id", "name", "segment", "eff_start_date", "eff_end_date", "is_current"]]
    result["customer_id"] = result["customer_id"].astype("int64")
    result["is_current"] = result["is_current"].astype("int64")
    result["eff_start_date"] = pd.to_datetime(result["eff_start_date"])
    result["eff_end_date"] = pd.to_datetime(result["eff_end_date"])

    return {"dim_customer_out": result}
